title: CYCLIC-HALFTRIM: lower-order integer boost trim with retained root-log memory and sample bounds

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), the single CYCLIC-HALFTRIM algorithm in proof.md, rootlog_base.md and cyclic_base.md recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 from independent ideal copies. Jointly on every execution branch, its total charged sequential work T is O(n^3 2^J(n)). Here J(n)=a sqrt(n)+(20/7)sqrt(n)/(log2 n)-(1/3)sqrt(n)/(log2 n)^(3/2)+(1/64)sqrt(n)/(log2 n)^2 and F(n)=a sqrt(n)-2sqrt(n)/(log2 n)^(1/2)+3sqrt(n)/(log2 n), with exact Pell rational  from cyclic_base.md Section 0. These eventual positive representative envelopes are evaluated for n>=2^1024 and extended positively on the finite smaller prefix; correctness covers every N. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. The configuration fixes beta=3/64, kappa=2 and x=s=max(2,floor(mu/sqrt(ell)-beta mu/ell)), with counted exact rational ell and integer floor, and recomputes every actual decoder/extractor parameter, A_star, Q_star=8 A_star(G_odd+2a2)+2a2 and Qcap=1024 Q_star. Failed and discarded acquisitions count. The exact growth index is 1/2.

No positive malformed fraction or maximum possible tolerance is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
